title: Enrich route-decision spans with per-hop metrics, KV cache context, and fallback metadata
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a compact, queryable routing-decision span that captures per-hop timing, routing rationale (region score, tier preference), cache/KV cache context, and fallback model variant metadata so that SREs and PMs can reconstruct why a request ended up at a particular model/region and whether fallback logic ran. Background: Current decision logs capture only the final routing decision and a coarse reason. During incidents we cannot correlate decisions with token-level latency spikes, cache effectiveness, or multi-hop routing where requests are proxied between region gateways. This ticket scopes the runtime and tracing changes to: 1) define a stable, low-cardinality span/schema for each routing hop and the final decision; 2) attach KV cache hit/miss counts and prefix cache keys used (hashed) to each hop; 3) record the scoring vector used for region selection (region_score, latency_estimate_ms, capacity_score, cost_score) as a compressed list; 4) include fallback metadata when model variants are substituted (original_model, chosen_variant, substitution_reason, degradation_metric); 5) emit an opaque trace_id and decision_id for correlation across observability, billing, and request logs. Constraints: keep per-decision payload small (<= 1KB avg) to limit telemetry cost; avoid PII and full prompts—only store metadata and hashed identifiers; make fields optional and sampled for high-throughput customers. Acceptance criteria: - Decision spans emitted for 100% of routed requests in canary region with sampling for full payloads at 10% - Each span includes a per-hop latency_ms, hop_role (selector, proxy, executor), and kv_cache_{hits,misses} - Fallback cases must include original_model and fallback_reason with a consistent enum - New fields available in Kibana/Traces dashboard with derived fields for region, tier, and fallback_count - Query for "requests where routing latency > 200ms and fallback_count > 0" returns results in < 5s on production index. Implementation notes: - We'll add a new light-weight protobuf/span schema in runtime (trace.v2.RoutingDecision) and a mapping layer to convert to existing trace ingestion. For rollouts, we will stub full-schema in the canary and fall back to legacy key for older runtimes. - Telemetry emission will be gated behind a feature-flag (observability.enhanced_routing_spans) and sampled parameter (observability.enhanced_routing_sampling_rate). - To protect privacy, store prompt_hash and cache_key_hash (SHA256 base64) instead of raw prompt or keys. - Store numeric scoring vector as an array of small ints after normalization (0-100) to reduce verbosity. - Provide a compatibility sham in Console to translate legacy decision logs into the new schema for dashboards. Notes on storage: compress score vectors with delta encoding and store as comma-separated string in decision span to satisfy flat-schema ingestion. Cost estimate: based on current throughput (1.2M routing-decisions/day), full payload at 100% would add ~3GB/day. Proposed default sampling for full spans: 10% (approx 300MB/day), with lightweight indexable records for 100% (decision_id, region, tier, fallback_flag).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary region emits enriched routing spans for 100% of requests with full spans sampled at 10%. 2) Per-hop metrics (latency_ms, hop_role, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses) are present and populated. 3) Fallback events populate original_model, chosen_variant, and substitution_reason enums. 4) Kibana/Traces dashboard surfaces derived fields and supports queries with <5s latency against production index. 5) Telemetry payloads remain <1.5KB median and do not contain raw prompts/PII.
data_retention_estimate: Hot indexed spans: 7d; cold compressed blobs: 90d; decision_id-only index: 365d
telemetry_cost_estimate: $2000/month at 1M full spans/day; ~$150/month at default 10% sampling (300MB/day)
rollout_plan: 1) Implement protobuf schema and runtime hook behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to canary region (us-west-2) with sampling=100% for light records, 10% for full payload. 3) Validate dashboards and query latency. 4) Expand to EU region and selected customers. 5) Enable for all regions after 2 weeks of monitoring and cost validation.
